Messages.Author: Mindy H Peeling-dykman
Messages.Body:
I was going through my Vampire: the masquerade, and found something that
kinda bothered me. Wake with evenings freshness was a thurmaturgy ritual.
Now if this card req'd the thurmaturgy discipline in Jyhad it would be
similar to rats warming, or other cards that allow certain vampires to
untap one way or another. As it is it's common, costs no blood, and can
be used by any vampire, which I think is a bit much. Am I alone in my
thoughts the Wake with Evening Freshness should be a Thurmaturgy card, or
do others think so also?

Messages.Author: Brian Wilson
Messages.Body:



I think that being able to block an action even though tapped (Wake
doesn't actually untap the vampire - it just blocks or reacts as if it
were untapped) is too important to be restricted by discipline, and I
would guess that the game designers felt the same way. Note that Rat's
Warning can only be used against bleed actions, so it's more limited than
a Wake, and limited by discipline (Animalism).

While Jyhad is based on Vampire: The Masquerade, we should avoid making
too many assumptions about the rules from one dictating the rules from
the other, as WotC has been quick to point out. Certainly some
compromises had to be made along the way. I think that this particular
compromise works well for all players, no matter how it treats the
Masquerade rule book.

Keep in mind, too, that many Jyhad players (myself included) don't play
Vampire and don't plan to, so that fine points like this one, while
interesting to read, don't influence our game play much.
